$narration: Spoken lines. One entry becomes one SRT cue and one synthesised audio segment. Keep each under 14 seconds so the subtitle stays readable.

narration.text: A response vehicle drives out of coverage. The network changes; the session should not.
Everything here is a software simulation. No radios, no satellite, no hardware.
The reactive baseline waits for its link to fail. The session goes dark four times: seven point three two seconds.
CONTINUA is the working application around that problem. Every panel reads from one engine over a live socket, and the execution mode is always on screen.
Five steps. Observe: receiver side facts only. The controller never sees the world's script.
Predict: a short horizon on those same facts, three seconds ahead.
Prepare: it warms cellular while Wi-Fi still carries. Steer: six tenths of a second later.
Explain: it records why, at the moment it decided.
Same seed, same trace, only the policy changed. Seven point three two seconds becomes zero point one six, and that remainder is the session starting up.
On the satellite route it holds the session through the fallback, and spends four point eight megabytes of satellite where the baseline spends forty seven.
Twenty paired trials say something we did not expect. Preparation is what removes the interruption. Take the predictor out and almost nothing changes.
What CONTINUA adds is the price: the same continuity at a third of the cost, a twelfth of the satellite data. It loses on application health.
Scope. A simulation, not a network. Emulation is unverified here and the kernel has no MPTCP. Total loss: ten point six seconds, every policy.
CONTINUA. Predictive network continuity. By Team Kanban.
